class autostorage.models.TimestampMixin(**data: Any)#

Bases: sqlmodel.SQLModel

Mixin adding server-managed creation/update timestamps.

Annotated as datetime | None since the value is unset in Python until the database fills it in via server_default/onupdate; nullable=False overrides the NULL-by-default column that an Optional annotation would otherwise produce, since the DB always has a value once the row is flushed.

class autostorage.models.GeometryRow(**data: Any)#

Bases: autostorage.models.BaseRow, automol.Geometry

Molecular geometry definition and metadata.

Variables:

  • symbols – Atomic symbols in order.

  • coordinates – Atomic coordinates in Angstrom.

  • charge – Total molecular charge.

  • spin – Number of unpaired electrons (2S).

  • geometry_hash – Content hash of symbols/coordinates/charge/spin, used to reject exactly-duplicate geometries (see find_or_create).

  • energies – Energy results computed at this geometry.

  • gradients – Gradient results computed at this geometry.

  • hessians – Hessian results computed at this geometry.

  • stationary_points – Stationary points defined by this geometry.

  • trajectory_links – Raw link rows connecting this geometry to trajectories.

  • calculation_links – Raw link rows connecting this geometry to calculations.

class autostorage.models.StationaryPointRow(**data: Any)#

Bases: autostorage.models.BaseRow

A stationary point on a potential energy surface.

Variables:

  • geometry_id – Foreign key to the underlying molecular geometry.

  • calculation_id – Foreign key to the calculation that identified this point.

  • order – Hessian index (0 for minima, 1 for first-order saddle points).

  • is_pseudo – Whether this point is not a true stationary point (e.g. constrained).

  • is_valid – Whether order agrees with the consensus order of its geometry’s Hessians (see autostorage.events.revalidate_geometry_orders_on_insert_update).

  • geometry – Geometry defining the coordinates of this point.

  • calculation – Calculation that identified this point.

  • identities – Chemical identifiers (e.g. InChI, SMILES) for this point.

  • stages – Reaction stages this stationary point belongs to.

classmethod find_or_create(db: autostorage.database.Database, *, geometry: autostorage.models.GeometryRow, calculation: autostorage.models.CalculationRow, order: int = 0, is_pseudo: bool = False, commit: bool = True) → Self#

Return the matching stationary point, creating and saving one if absent.

Matches on (geometry, calculation): reusing a match means it’s the same computed point, so order/is_pseudo are only used when creating a new row.

Parameters:

  • commit – If True (default), commit a newly-created row immediately. If False, only flush it (still assigns .id), leaving the caller’s transaction open – for a caller staging several dedup lookups that must succeed or fail together.

  • optional – If True (default), commit a newly-created row immediately. If False, only flush it (still assigns .id), leaving the caller’s transaction open – for a caller staging several dedup lookups that must succeed or fail together.

identity(*, kind: str | None = None, algorithm: Any | None = None) → IdentityRow | None#

Return the first loaded identity matching kind and/or algorithm.

Searches self.identities (the already-loaded relationship list), not the database — use StationaryPointRow.query for a DB lookup.

classmethod find_or_create(db: autostorage.database.Database, *, program: str, method: str, program_version: str | None = None, basis: str | None = None, commit: bool = True) → Self#

Return the matching model row, creating and saving one if absent.

unique_model doesn’t catch duplicates when program_version or basis is NULL, since SQL treats NULL as distinct from itself in unique constraints. Callers that don’t always supply both should use this instead of constructing and adding a ModelRow directly, to avoid silently accumulating duplicate rows for the same model.

Parameters:

  • commit – If True (default), commit a newly-created row immediately. If False, only flush it (still assigns .id), leaving the caller’s transaction open — for a caller staging several dedup lookups that must succeed or fail together.

  • optional – If True (default), commit a newly-created row immediately. If False, only flush it (still assigns .id), leaving the caller’s transaction open — for a caller staging several dedup lookups that must succeed or fail together.

classmethod find_or_create(db: autostorage.database.Database, *, model: autostorage.models.ModelRow, calc_type: autostorage.types.CalcType, input_provenance: dict[str, Any] | None = None, status: autostorage.types.CalcStatus = CalcStatus.PENDING, error_message: str | None = None, output_provenance: dict[str, Any] | None = None, commit: bool = True) → Self#

Return the matching calculation row, creating and saving one if absent.

Matches on (model, calc_type, input_provenance) – the job that was run – ignoring status/error_message/output_provenance, which describe outcome rather than identity, so they’re only used when creating a new row.

Parameters:

  • commit – If True (default), commit a newly-created row immediately. If False, only flush it (still assigns .id), leaving the caller’s transaction open – for a caller staging several dedup lookups that must succeed or fail together.

  • optional – If True (default), commit a newly-created row immediately. If False, only flush it (still assigns .id), leaving the caller’s transaction open – for a caller staging several dedup lookups that must succeed or fail together.
